prediction.separate_gravity: d<K>/dE = -1.00 +- 0.05 after re-virialisation (virial theorem, Lynden-Bell 1999); with Plummer softening the virial value is K = E*w/(w-2), w = <W_soft>/<U_soft> (Mentat solve_equation), i.e. -w/(2-w), about -0.99 for eps = 0.02 b
prediction.same_gas: d<K>/dE >= 0 (+1 for an ideal gas at fixed volume; C_gas = (3/2) N k_B = 2.65e-21 J/K at N = 128)

prereg.protocol_as_designed: Plummer N = 128, M = 1e12 kg, b = 5 km, eps = 0.02 b, dt = t_cross/300 with t_cross := sqrt(b^3/(G M)) (the sketch's definition), velocity-Verlet NBodySystem.step; seeds 1, 2, 3 with the sketch's sampler; relax 10 t_cross (3000 steps); inject by scaling peculiar velocities by (1+delta), delta in {-0.10, -0.05, 0, +0.05, +0.10}, from the SAME relaxed state; integrate int(3 t_relax/dt) = 2374 steps with t_relax = 2.638 t_cross (Mentat); <K> over samples with k*dt > 2 t_relax (the sketch's window); dE = ((1+delta)^2 - 1) K0.
prereg.primary_statistic: raw slope per seed = np.polyfit(dE, <K>_delta - <K>_0, 1)[0] over delta in {-0.10, -0.05, +0.05, +0.10}, all particles, pre-registered window; then mean and sample std (ddof = 1) over the 3 seeds

pass_fail_fixed.SEPARATE: mean raw slope in [-1.10, -0.90] AND seed std <= 0.05 AND softened-energy drift <= 1e-4
pass_fail_fixed.UNRESOLVED: mean slope in (-0.90, 0), or in the band but a std/drift gate fails, or below -1.10 (negative but off the prediction); reported as such, never rounded into a pass
pass_fail_fixed.drift_metric: end-point |E_soft(end)/E_soft(start) - 1| of every integrated segment (relax and each branch), maximum over segments; the max-over-time excursion is reported alongside

prereg.gate_before_injection: over the last 5 t_cross of relax: 2<K>/|<W_soft>| in [0.97, 1.03] AND |<2K + W_soft> - (1/2)[Idot]/T| / |<W_soft>| <= 1e-3 (trapezoid time averages, samples every step)
secondary_analyses_declared_now: LJ-corrected slope: K_LJ = <K> - (1/4)[Idot]/T per window (equals -<W_soft>/2 by the Lagrange-Jacobi identity), slope as above
bound-only slope: <K_bound> (particles with e_i = v^2/2 + phi_soft,i < 0) vs the same dE

EXTENDED window, same thresholds: each branch is integrated on to 6 t_relax (int(6 t_relax/dt) = 4749 steps); <K> over k in [2374, 4749). Declared now because the design's t_cross = sqrt(b^3/GM) is 6.26x shorter than the Heggie-Mathieu crossing time (Mentat (3pi/32)^(-3/2)) and the design's post-injection run (7.9 units) is only 0.60 of the orbital period at the half-mass radius (Mentat orbital_period 13.24 units) -- the pre-registered window may sit inside the breathing oscillation. The extended window is the corrected-criterion analysis; the original stays the primary.
time-resolved slope: running mean of <K> over one design t_relax, slope from the four branches at each time (figure)
prereg.could_it_fail: Yes in the sense of the design's three outcomes: SAME would need the injected energy to stay kinetic (the t = 0+ slope is +1 by construction); UNRESOLVED if the cluster has not re-virialised inside the window or escapers/drift spoil it. But a slope of -1 is the virial theorem for any bound, stationary 1/r system: a pass validates that the engine integrates 1/r gravity and that the window is long enough, and adds no evidence beyond the theorem itself about whether gravity and gas thermodynamics are one phenomenon.

headline_v2: Adding energy to a gate-passing N = 128 Plummer cluster lowered its mean kinetic energy in all 12 kicked branches: d<K>/dE = -1.04 +- 0.13 (seed SEM; seed std 0.22; per seed -0.82, -1.27, -1.03) in the pre-registered window, against +1 for an ideal gas (a formula, not a simulation). The pre-registered verdict is UNRESOLVED because the seed std exceeds the 0.05 limit; the extended window (3 to 4.74 design t_relax, cut short of 6) gives -1.36 +- 0.15, also UNRESOLVED. The kicked clusters' moment of inertia is still growing relative to the control at 12.5 design units in every seed and the branches decorrelate after about 2-3 units, so no turnaround, breathing period or damping was measured. By the energy plus Lagrange-Jacobi identity the miss from -1 sits, by construction, in the non-stationarity term (-0.050) plus a softening term (+0.011). This validates the virial theorem's sign on the engine; it is not evidence for the unification thesis.
design_corrections_v2: Time unit. The design's t_cross = sqrt(b^3/GM) = 43277 s is shorter than every standard crossing time of a Plummer sphere (Mentat simplify_expr): 3.13x shorter than R_V/v_rms, 2.40x shorter than r_half/v_rms (the half-diameter R/v crossing time that goes with t_relax = 0.1 N/lnN t_cross; the textbook derivation gives N/(8 lnN) = 3.30 at N = 128 against 0.1 N/lnN = 2.64), and 6.26x shorter than the Heggie-Mathieu full-diameter t_cr = 2 R_V/v_rms. So the design's 3 t_relax run is 0.96 (R_V) to 1.25 (r_half) relaxation times in the matching convention, and 0.48 only in the Heggie-Mathieu convention (v1 quoted only 0.48). Convention-free: the pre-registered window is 2.63 design units = 0.20, and the whole post-kick run 0.94, of the circular-orbit period at r_half (13.24 units, Mentat orbital_period), so phase mixing after the kick cannot be complete.

Seed-std gate. The gate is on the per-seed std, so adding seeds cannot meet it; only lower per-seed scatter can. The observed scatter (0.222 pre-registered) has two candidate sources this run cannot apportion: (i) fast finite-N fluctuations of branches that have decorrelated (relax-phase K, integrated autocorrelation time 0.5-1.2 units) predict 0.08/0.07/0.03 per seed, about the within-seed 4-point scatter (rms SE 0.086); (ii) slow, seed-specific evolution of K over several units (control-branch K over 1-12.5 units, tau_int 1.4-2.1 units) predicts 0.27/0.20/0.13, about the observed scatter. Between-seed vs within-seed variance: F = 6.6 (p = 0.031, F(2,6)) in the pre-registered window only; F = 1.08 (ext) and 0.02 (long), so no robust seed-level excess after allowing for the four windows examined. Cutting the scatter about 4.4x to 0.05 needs, by noise scaling, about 20x longer windows (about 50 design units, 4 T_orb(r_half)) or N of order 2,500; delta cannot be raised much (delta = 0.2 already injects 0.44 K0). And since the kicked clusters were still expanding at 12.5 units, a longer window would also have to wait for the expansion to finish. Alternatives: state the criterion on the seed SEM, or on the coherent pre-decorrelation phase. The v1 rationale ('several breathing periods, >~ 40 units') is withdrawn: no breathing period was measured.

The design's 'LJ-corrected' K_LJ = <K> - (1/4)[Idot]/T equals -<W_s>/2 and removes only half of the non-stationarity term L = (1/2)[Idot]/T; removing all of it (<K> - L) returns -1 + d<U_s - W_s>/dE by construction (-0.989 +- 0.003). The decomposition <K> = -E + L + <U_s - W_s> is an identity [BY CONSTRUCTION] for any finite window of a conservative pairwise system: it books every departure from the virial value as L, whether it comes from a coherent mode or from noise, so it cannot identify a mechanism. Its non-trivial content is narrow: the softening term is only +0.011 (pre) / +0.015 (ext), the energy slope is 1.000005 (injection exact), and the identity closes to <= 4e-5. The raw slope is the test.

Against the original criterion: pre-registered window UNRESOLVED (mean -1.039 in band, seed std 0.222 > 0.05, end-point drift 2.8e-05 passes); SAME excluded (seed mean below zero at t = 8.1, 2 dof, one-sided p = 0.0074). Against the corrected criterion (extended window, same thresholds): UNRESOLVED (-1.356 +- 0.145, below -1.10). Post hoc, the longest window (2-4.74 t_relax) gives -1.24 +- 0.05 (error from the within-seed fit SEs; the 3-seed std 0.011 is a small-sample accident, 95% CI on sigma [0.006, 0.071]).
The design leaves 'drift' undefined. The pre-registered end-point drift passes (2.8e-05); the max-over-time excursion (2.1e-04) would fail a strict reading.

The gate is a 5-unit time average and passes (1.020, 1.016, 1.005), but it does not make the cluster virialised at the kick: the instantaneous 2K/|W_s| at injection was 1.094, 0.981, 0.962, it ranged 0.93-1.10, 0.97-1.07, 0.96-1.06 inside the gate windows, and the delta = 0 controls swing over 0.93-1.15, 0.96-1.13, 0.96-1.07. 'Relaxed' is replaced by 'gate-passing'.

The softened-virial value K = E w/(w-2) (Mentat solve_equation), -0.9952 here, holds at fixed w and leaves out E dw/dE. The consistent expectation including dw/dE is -1 + d<U_s - W_s>/dE = -0.989 (pre) / -0.985 (ext).

Withdrawn from v1: 'a coherent and slowly damped breathing oscillation, not sampling noise' and 'the 13-unit breathing period'. 13.24 units is the Kepler period at r_half (Mentat), a proxy, never a measured period. Measured instead: the moment-of-inertia response (dI/dE)|E|/I0 rises at every step after 1 unit in all seeds, reaching 1.62, 2.30, 1.11 at 12.5 units (homologous re-virialised value 2); dIdot/dE stays positive throughout, peaking at 7.5, 4.5, 5.1 units, so in the extended window the expansion is decelerating, which by Lagrange-Jacobi puts 2K + W_s below zero and <K> below the virial value (10 of 12 branch responses below -1 there). The half-mass radius response levels off after 5-9 units near the homologous value 1 (seeds 2, 3: 0.78 and 0.83 at 12 units) or above it (seed 1: 1.63). The Plummer I integrand goes as 1/x at large r (Mentat series_expansion), so I is halo-weighted: the halo is still expanding.

modified_or_rejected: X1 (S2) Not adopted as stated: 'the seed spread (0.22) matches finite-N K-fluctuation noise (about 0.2 per seed)'. Reason: S2's model block-averaged the whole relax phase, including the initial-relaxation transient. It also multiplied by sqrt(2) for the control's noise, but that noise is common to all four points and goes into the intercept, not the slope. Recomputed with integrated autocorrelation times: fast fluctuations (relax-phase K) predict 0.08/0.07/0.03 per seed, matching the within-seed 4-point scatter (rms 0.086) but not the spread. Only slow, multi-unit variation of the control's K predicts 0.27/0.20/0.13, which is about the spread. Between-seed vs within-seed F = 6.6 (p = 0.03) in the pre window only. The text now says the run cannot apportion the spread between finite-N noise and seed-specific slow evolution.

X2 (S2) Adopted with a correction: 'coherent and approaches -1 within about 5 units'. In the 3-5 unit window the slope is -0.83 +- 0.06 (std), not yet -1, and the responses are monotone in delta (coherent, but nonlinear in delta). The seed-mean instantaneous slope reaches -0.97 at 5-6 units.

X3 (S2) Adopted in measured form: 'describe the extended overshoot as non-stationary halo expansion plus finite-N noise'. In the extended window dIdot/dE is past its maximum in every seed, so the expansion is decelerating, which by Lagrange-Jacobi puts <K> below the virial value. 10 of 12 branch responses are below -1 there. How much is noise cannot be separated with 3 seeds.

X4 (S1) Qualified: 'the kicked clusters are still expanding'. This holds for the halo-weighted moment of inertia (log-divergent Plummer integrand, Mentat series 1/x). The half-mass-radius response levels off after 5-9 units near (seeds 2, 3) or above (seed 1) the homologous value. So the wording is now 'the moment of inertia is still growing'.

X5 No new simulation. None of the required changes needs one. Completing the planned extension to 6 t_relax would mean re-integrating all 15 branches from the relaxed states, because the branch files store diagnostics, not phase-space states. That is about 90 min on this shared machine, so it was not done and is flagged as the natural follow-up.
